newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks led up by banks, cement, food.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks led up by banks, cement, food.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged up on Monday, led by banks, cement and foods in sessions where trading volume was concentrated in brewing giant Bavaria.
Bogota's IBB index was up 0.2 percent to 1,032.9 amid a 652 million peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.66 percent to 16,182.08 amid a 2 billion peso trade.

"The market was quiet today because of the absence of foreign funds (due to the U.S. Presidents Day holiday). There were a number of cross deals and some speculation because the central bank closed 90 day deposits which is likely to force down interst rates," one Bogota trader said.

Last Friday the central bank announced it was temporarily suspending its 90 day fixed term deposits which were giving a return equivalent to 25 percent annually. The broker said the anticipated fall in interest rates was pushing traditional fixed income investors into the stock market.
The main volume in Bogota was centered on a 344 million peso cross deal in Bavaria, unchanged at 6,700 pesos per share, and a 1.02 billion cross deal at the same price on the Medellin exchange.
Banco de Colombia rose 1.43 percent to 425 on the Bogota exchange while Banco de Bogota closed up 0.79 percent at 6,350.
"There are high expectations for Banco de Bogota profits, that's what pushed up the price," said another Bogota broker.

In Medellin, food manufacturer Industrias Alimenticias Noel, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueo conglomerate, rose 2.6 percent to 3,950. Cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, part of the same conglomerate, rose 2.36 percent to 5,630 while Banco de Bogota rose 1.42 percent to 6,399.5.
